items.action: Patch internet-facing PHP to a fixed release now and check for signs of compromise; treat Apache mod_php as highest risk.
items.details: Both are unauthenticated remote code execution flaws (CVSS 9.2 each) in PHP's request handling. Fixed releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; CISA directs agencies that cannot patch immediately to take PHP systems offline.
items.summary: CISA added PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 26, classifying them as exploited in the wild.
items.title: CISA adds PHP2Shell flaws to KEV; federal deadline Oct 29

items.action: Apply the PAN-OS hotfix for your branch and update Node.js runtimes and Brotli libraries to patched versions.
items.details: The out-of-bounds write in Google Brotli lets a remote unauthenticated attacker corrupt decoder memory, disclose memory contents, cause denial of service, or potentially execute code. Node.js patched the same flaw in 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; PAN-OS 11.1 and 10.2 are not affected.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks confirmed on Oct 26 that the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 9.2) affects PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2.
items.title: Node2Shell Brotli flaw confirmed in PAN-OS; patch now

items.action: Upgrade self-managed GitLab to the fixed build for your release line, starting with internet-facing servers; Oct 12 patch builds are still vulnerable.
items.details: An integer overflow in the Onigmo regex engine, reached by rendering a crafted .org file, affects self-managed GitLab CE/EE back to version 7.0. Fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6 and backports to 18.11.13; GitLab.com is already patched.
items.summary: GitLab's CVE-2026-110264, rated CVSS 10.0, lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on self-managed GitLab servers and was reiterated in Oct 26 threat briefings.
items.title: GitLab CVSS 10.0 flaw still top patch priority

items.action: Patch known-exploited edge flaws, enforce MFA on VPNs, segment networks, and keep offline, immutable backups with tested recovery.
items.details: SafePay gains access via stolen or guessed credentials, phishing and brute force, plus five older edge-device flaws in Cisco ASA, Veeam and SonicWall gear. Operators use legitimate admin tools, steal data, encrypt files with a .SafePay extension, and deliberately destroy backups including shadow copies.
items.summary: US, German and UK agencies' joint advisory AA26-293A (Oct 20) ties SafePay ransomware to at least 600 victims across critical-infrastructure sectors since August 2024.
items.title: SafePay ransomware hit at least 600 victims, joint advisory warns

items.action: Treat legal-sector leak-site listings as exposure risk: monitor for client data exposure and review third-party and vendor access.
items.details: The listing was tracked via ransomware.live; no technical details on initial access, affected systems or data scope have been published, and the claim itself is unverified by the firm.
items.summary: Silentransomgroup listed New York law firm Morrison Cohen on its leak site on Oct 26, 2026, in a double-extortion ransomware claim.
items.title: Law firm Morrison Cohen listed by Silentransomgroup

items.action: Rotate long-lived service and machine accounts, audit admin-side accounts, and revoke stale credentials.
items.details: The group alleges entry via an unrotated internal machine account with admin reach, following a separate hot-wallet incident; the claim and figures are unverified.
items.summary: Whitearmor claims to hold Gamdom's full user database — 15,420,003 accounts — and is demanding $15 million in BTC, per an Oct 27 report of the Oct 26 claim.
items.title: Gamdom hit by Whitearmor claim: 15.4M accounts alleged

items.action: Check for reliance on affected eMudhra intermediates and replace certificates as directed; do not dismiss the issue because browsers updated.
items.details: CERT-In said affected keys had values smaller than 256, making them easy to recover. eMudhra said it found no infrastructure or customer-data compromise, that its signature and eSign services were unaffected, and that browsers blocked the affected certificates.
items.summary: On Oct 26, Indian trust provider eMudhra apologised after a script error produced weak private keys for eight intermediate certificate authorities, including one with a numerical value of just four.
items.title: eMudhra apologises over weak certificate keys

items.action: Public-sector teams should prioritise PHP patching and compromise checks on all internet-facing portals.
items.details: State government portals, district sites, municipal services and grievance systems widely rely on PHP-based CMSs and frameworks, making the PHP2Shell flaws a broad exposure for public services.
items.summary: Cert-In is coordinating with state IT departments to patch thousands of government websites against the critical PHP flaws, officials told The Economic Times on Oct 27.
items.title: Cert-In and states rush to patch PHP flaws on govt portals

items.action: Monitor for corroboration or official comment before treating this as a confirmed incident.
items.details: The report provides no independently verified evidence of a compromise, affected systems, data involved or publication — treat it as an early-warning indicator, not a confirmed breach.
items.summary: ThreatMon reported on Oct 26 that ScarlettGroup claimed Rajasthan Police as a new victim; no systems, data or intrusion details have been confirmed.
items.title: ScarlettGroup claims Rajasthan Police as victim (unverified)
